note: CLN3-associated nonsyndromic retinitis pigmentosa (RP101) is consistently linked to non-classical genotypes, such as missense or splice-altering variants in trans with the common 1.02-kb deletion or homozygous missense variants, sparing systemic neurological symptoms seen in classical JNCL.

evidence.text: Biallelic CLN3 variants cause either juvenile-onset neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (JNCL) or isolated retinal dystrophy; most JNCL patients carry the common 1.02-kb deletion variant homozygously, whereas missense variants have been identified in isolated nonsyndromic retinal dystrophy without neurological signs.

source.title: Novel homozygous CLN3 missense variant in isolated retinal dystrophy: A case report and electron microscopic findings
source.quote: Biallelic CLN3 gene variants have been found in either juvenile-onset neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (JNCL) or isolated retinal dystrophy. It has been reported that most JNCL patients carry a common 1.02-kb deletion variant homozygously.

numbers.metric: duration of follow-up without neurological signs (years)

evidence.text: A patient presenting with late-onset, non-syndromic retinal dystrophy without systemic neurological involvement was found to have compound heterozygous CLN3 mutations consisting of the classical 1.02-kb deletion and an exonic splicing/missense mutation (c.175G>A).

source.title: Clinical and molecular characterization of non-syndromic retinal dystrophy due to c.175G>A mutation in ceroid lipofuscinosis neuronal 3 (CLN3)
source.quote: Genetic testing revealed compound heterozygous CLN3 mutations: the 1.02 kb deletion and a novel missense mutation (c.175G>A). In silico, analyses predicted the c.175G>A mutation disrupted an exonic splice enhancer site in exon 3.
